BATCH-20260519-194136-38FA7C.prompt: We are setting up Zendesk for a company called BrightWave Internet Services. They are a fibre internet provider with three support teams: Technical Support, Billing Support, and Cancellations.  Please create the following:  1. Three ticket fields:    - A dropdown called "Issue Category" with options: Connection Issue,      Speed Problem, Billing Query, Contract Question, Cancellation Request    - A dropdown called "Service Type" with options: Fibre 10MB, Fibre 50MB,      Fibre 100MB, Business Fibre    - A text field called "Account Reference Number"  2. Three triggers:    - When a ticket is created and Issue Category is "Billing Query",      assign it to the Billing Support team and add tag "billing"    - When a ticket is created and Issue Category is "Cancellation Request",      assign it to the Cancellations team, add tag "cancellation",      and set priority to High    - When a ticket is created and Issue Category is "Connection Issue",      assign it to Technical Support and add tag "technical"  3. Three views:    - All open Billing Support tickets assigned to the Billing Support team    - All open Cancellation tickets with High priority    - All unassigned Technical Support tickets  4. Three macros:    - A macro called "Acknowledge Billing Query" that sends a reply:      "Thank you for contacting BrightWave Billing Support. We have received      your query and will respond within 24 hours." and adds tag "billing_acknowledged"    - A macro called "Escalate to Cancellations" that assigns the ticket to      the Cancellations team, sets priority to High, and adds tag "escalated"    - A macro called "Request Account Number" that sends a reply:      "To assist you further, please provide your BrightWave account reference      number." and adds tag "awaiting_account_number"  5. One ticket form:    - A form called "BrightWave Support Form" that includes the following      fields in order: Subject, Description, Issue Category, Service Type,      Account Reference Number, Priority

BATCH-20260521-152947-DBA3ED.prompt: We are setting up Zendesk for a company called PeakCare Medical Supplies. They supply medical equipment and consumables to hospitals, clinics, and  private practitioners across South Africa. They have four support teams:  Order Support, Technical Support, Returns and Repairs, and Accounts.  Please create the following:  1. Four ticket fields:    - A dropdown called "Request Type" with options: New Order Inquiry,      Order Status Check, Damaged Item, Equipment Fault, Return Request,      Invoice Query, Account Update    - A dropdown called "Customer Type" with options: Hospital, Private Clinic,      General Practitioner, Pharmacy, Government Facility    - A dropdown called "Product Category" with options: Diagnostic Equipment,      Surgical Consumables, Patient Monitoring, Mobility Aids, Wound Care    - A text field called "Order Reference Number"  2. Four triggers:    - When a ticket is created and Request Type is "Equipment Fault",      assign it to Technical Support, add tag "equipment_fault",      and set priority to High    - When a ticket is created and Request Type is "Return Request",      assign it to Returns and Repairs, add tag "return_requested",      and set priority to Normal    - When a ticket is created and Request Type is "Invoice Query",      assign it to Accounts, add tag "invoice_query"    - When a ticket is created and Customer Type is "Hospital" and      Request Type is "Damaged Item", assign to Returns and Repairs,      add tag "hospital_damage_claim", and set priority to Urgent  3. Four views:    - All open Equipment Fault tickets assigned to Technical Support      sorted by oldest first    - All Urgent tickets assigned to Returns and Repairs    - All open Invoice Query tickets assigned to Accounts    - All unassigned tickets across all teams sorted by creation date  4. BATCH-20260521-194142-972E60.prompt: We are setting up Zendesk for a company called PeakCare Medical Supplies. They supply medical equipment and consumables to hospitals, clinics, and  private practitioners across South Africa. They have four support teams:  Order Support, Technical Support, Returns and Repairs, and Accounts.  Please create the following:  1. Four ticket fields:    - A dropdown called "Request Type" with options: New Order Inquiry,      Order Status Check, Damaged Item, Equipment Fault, Return Request,      Invoice Query, Account Update    - A dropdown called "Customer Type" with options: Hospital, Private Clinic,      General Practitioner, Pharmacy, Government Facility    - A dropdown called "Product Category" with options: Diagnostic Equipment,      Surgical Consumables, Patient Monitoring, Mobility Aids, Wound Care    - A text field called "Order Reference Number"  2. Four triggers:    - When a ticket is created and Request Type is "Equipment Fault",      assign it to Technical Support, add tag "equipment_fault",      and set priority to High    - When a ticket is created and Request Type is "Return Request",      assign it to Returns and Repairs, add tag "return_requested",      and set priority to Normal    - When a ticket is created and Request Type is "Invoice Query",      assign it to Accounts, add tag "invoice_query"    - When a ticket is created and Customer Type is "Hospital" and      Request Type is "Damaged Item", assign to Returns and Repairs,      add tag "hospital_damage_claim", and set priority to Urgent  3. Four views:    - All open Equipment Fault tickets assigned to Technical Support      sorted by oldest first    - All Urgent tickets assigned to Returns and Repairs    - All open Invoice Query tickets assigned to Accounts    - All unassigned tickets across all teams sorted by creation date  4. Three macros:    - A macro called "Acknowledge Equipment Fault" that sends a reply:      "Thank you for contacting PeakCare Technical Support. We have logged      your equipment fault and a technician will be in touch within 4 hours."      and adds tag "fault_acknowledged"    - A macro called "Request Order Reference" that sends a reply:      "To locate your order, please provide your PeakCare order reference      number so we can assist you further." and adds tag "awaiting_order_ref"    - A macro called "Escalate to Urgent" that sets priority to Urgent,      assigns to Returns and Repairs, and adds tag "urgent_escalation"  5. Two ticket forms:    - A form called "PeakCare General Support Form" that includes fields      in order: Subject, Description, Request Type, Customer Type,      Order Reference Number, Priority    - A form called "PeakCare Equipment Fault Form" that includes fields      in order: Subject, Description, Request Type, Product Category,      Customer Type, Order Reference Number, Priority

They supply medical equipment and consumables to hospitals, clinics, and  private practitioners across South Africa. They have four support teams:  Order Support, Technical Support, Returns and Repairs, and Accounts.  Please create the following:  1. Four ticket fields:    - A dropdown called "Request Type" with options: New Order Inquiry,      Order Status Check, Damaged Item, Equipment Fault, Return Request,      Invoice Query, Account Update    - A dropdown called "Customer Type" with options: Hospital, Private Clinic,      General Practitioner, Pharmacy, Government Facility    - A dropdown called "Product Category" with options: Diagnostic Equipment,      Surgical Consumables, Patient Monitoring, Mobility Aids, Wound Care    - A text field called "Order Reference Number"  2. Four triggers:    - When a ticket is created and Request Type is "Equipment Fault",      assign it to Technical Support, add tag "equipment_fault",      and set priority to High    - When a ticket is created and Request Type is "Return Request",      assign it to Returns and Repairs, add tag "return_requested",      and set priority to Normal    - When a ticket is created and Request Type is "Invoice Query",      assign it to Accounts, add tag "invoice_query"    - When a ticket is created and Customer Type is "Hospital" and      Request Type is "Damaged Item", assign to Returns and Repairs,      add tag "hospital_damage_claim", and set priority to Urgent  3. Four views:    - All open Equipment Fault tickets assigned to Technical Support      sorted by oldest first    - All Urgent tickets assigned to Returns and Repairs    - All open Invoice Query tickets assigned to Accounts    - All unassigned tickets across all teams sorted by creation date  4. Three macros:    - A macro called "Acknowledge Equipment Fault" that sends a reply:      "Thank you for contacting PeakCare Technical Support. We have logged      your equipment fault and a technician will be in touch within 4 hours."      and adds tag "fault_acknowledged"    - A macro called "Request Order Reference" that sends a reply:      "To locate your order, please provide your PeakCare order reference      number so we can assist you further." and adds tag "awaiting_order_ref"    - A macro called "Escalate to Urgent" that sets priority to Urgent,      assigns to Returns and Repairs, and adds tag "urgent_escalation"  5. Two ticket forms:    - A form called "PeakCare General Support Form" that includes fields      in order: Subject, Description, Request Type, Customer Type,      Order Reference Number, Priority    - A form called "PeakCare Equipment Fault Form" that includes fields      in order: Subject, Description, Request Type, Product Category,      Customer Type, Order Reference Number, Priority

BATCH-20260522-200439-C17113.prompt: We are setting up Zendesk for a company called Vantage Wealth Management. They provide investment portfolios, retirement annuities, and financial  planning services to individual and corporate clients across South Africa. They have five support teams: Client Services, Compliance, Investments, Claims and Payouts, and IT Support.  Please create the following:  1. Five ticket fields:    - A dropdown called "Query Type" with options: Portfolio Statement Request,      Fund Switch Request, Withdrawal Request, Beneficiary Update,      Compliance Document Submission, System Access Issue, General Inquiry    - A dropdown called "Client Classification" with options: Individual Retail,      High Net Worth Individual, Corporate Client, Trust, Pension Fund    - A dropdown called "Product Type" with options: Unit Trust, Retirement Annuity,      Living Annuity, Tax Free Savings Account, Endowment Policy    - A dropdown called "Urgency Reason" with options: Legal Deadline,      Medical Emergency, Financial Hardship, Regulatory Requirement, Routine    - A text field called "Client Portfolio Number"  2. Five triggers:    - When a ticket is created and Query Type is "Withdrawal Request"      and Client Classification is "High Net Worth Individual",      assign to Claims and Payouts, add tag "hnw_withdrawal",      and set priority to High    - When a ticket is created and Query Type is "Compliance Document Submission",      assign to Compliance, add tag "compliance_submission",      and set priority to Normal    - When a ticket is created and Query Type is "Fund Switch Request",      assign to Investments, add tag "fund_switch"    - When a ticket is created and Urgency Reason is "Legal Deadline",      assign to Compliance, add tag "legal_deadline",      and set priority to Urgent    - When a ticket is created and Query Type is "System Access Issue",      assign to IT Support, add tag "system_access",      and set priority to High  3. Five views:    - All open Withdrawal Requests assigned to Claims and Payouts      sorted by priority descending    - All Urgent Compliance tickets sorted by oldest first    - All open Fund Switch Requests assigned to Investments    - All High Net Worth Individual tickets across all teams      sorted by creation date    - All unassigned tickets older than 24 hours across all teams  4. Four macros:    - A macro called "Acknowledge Withdrawal Request" that sends a reply:      "Thank you for submitting your withdrawal request to Vantage Wealth      Management. Your request has been received and will be processed      within 3 to 5 business days subject to compliance verification."      and adds tag "withdrawal_acknowledged"    - A macro called "Request Compliance Documents" that sends a reply:      "To process your request we require the following: a certified copy      of your identity document, proof of banking details, and a completed      FICA declaration form. Please upload these at your earliest convenience."      and adds tag "compliance_docs_requested"    - A macro called "Escalate to Legal Review" that assigns the ticket      to Compliance, sets priority to Urgent, adds tag "legal_review",      and adds an internal note: "This ticket has been flagged for legal      review due to a regulatory deadline or compliance requirement."    - A macro called "Request Portfolio Number" that sends a reply:      "To locate your account and assist you accurately, please provide      your Vantage client portfolio number." and adds tag "awaiting_portfolio_number"  5. Three ticket forms:    - A form called "Vantage Client Services Form" that includes fields      in order: Subject, Description, Query Type, Client Classification,      Product Type, Client Portfolio Number, Priority    - A form called "Vantage Withdrawal and Payout Form" that includes      fields in order: Subject, Description, Query Type, Client Classification,      Product Type, Urgency Reason, Client Portfolio Number, Priority    - A form called "Vantage Compliance Submission Form" that includes      fields in order: Subject, Description, Query Type, Client Classification,      Urgency Reason, Client Portfolio Number, Priority

We are setting up Zendesk for a company called Harvest Table Restaurants.
They operate a chain of family restaurants across South Africa. They have 
three support teams: Customer Experience, Reservations, and Franchise Support.

Please create the following:

1. Three ticket fields:
   - A dropdown called "Query Type" with options: Reservation Request,
     Complaint, Compliment, Franchise Inquiry, Catering Request,
     Gift Voucher Query, General Inquiry
   - A dropdown called "Restaurant Location" with options: Sandton,
     Cape Town Waterfront, Durban Umhlanga, Pretoria Menlyn,
     Port Elizabeth, Bloemfontein
   - A text field called "Booking Reference Number"

2. Three triggers:
   - When a ticket is created and Query Type is "Complaint",
     assign to Customer Experience, add tag "customer_complaint",
     and set priority to High
   - When a ticket is created and Query Type is "Reservation Request",
     assign to Reservations, add tag "reservation_request"
   - When a ticket is created and Query Type is "Franchise Inquiry",
     assign to Franchise Support, add tag "franchise_inquiry",
     and set priority to Normal

3. Three views:
   - All open Complaint tickets assigned to Customer Experience
     sorted by oldest first
   - All open Reservation Request tickets assigned to Reservations
     sorted by creation date
   - All unassigned tickets across all teams sorted by oldest first

4. Three macros:
   - A macro called "Acknowledge Complaint" that sends a reply:
     "Thank you for reaching out to Harvest Table Restaurants. We sincerely
     apologize for your experience and a member of our Customer Experience
     team will be in touch within 24 hours to resolve this for you."
     and adds tag "complaint_acknowledged"
   - A macro called "Request Booking Reference" that sends a reply:
     "To locate your reservation, please provide your Harvest Table booking
     reference number so we can assist you right away."
     and adds tag "awaiting_booking_ref"

BATCH-20260712-022823-3C5D3D.prompt:
Build a Zendesk support operating model for “Apex Mobility Finance”, a company that finances electric scooters, delivery e-bikes, and small EV fleets for gig workers and small businesses.

Business context:
Apex has these departments:
- Customer Support: first-line support for account questions, payment issues, login problems, and general requests.
- Claims & Incidents: handles damaged vehicles, theft reports, accident claims, insurance evidence, and urgent safety incidents.
- Finance Operations: handles failed payments, settlement disputes, refunds, payoff quotes, and billing corrections.
- Fleet Onboarding: helps business customers onboard multiple riders, verify documents, activate vehicles, and schedule handover.
- Technical Support: handles app bugs, GPS/device issues, charger problems, battery diagnostics, and telematics troubleshooting.
- Compliance: handles KYC document review, suspicious activity, regulatory complaints, and data/privacy requests.
- VIP / Enterprise Success: handles high-value fleet accounts, partner escalations, and white-glove support.

Create a complete Zendesk configuration in dependency order:
- Groups for the departments above, reusing existing matching groups if selected.
- Ticket fields for Department, Customer Segment, Vehicle Type, Issue Category, Incident Severity, Payment Status, KYC Status, Fleet Size, and Requested Outcome.
- Ticket forms for General Support, Claims & Incidents, Finance Operations, Fleet Onboarding, Technical Support, Compliance Review, and VIP Enterprise Support.
- Triggers to route tickets to the correct department based on form, issue category, customer segment, severity, and payment/KYC signals.
- Automations for stale urgent incidents, unresolved failed payments, pending KYC reviews, and enterprise escalations.
- Macros for first response, missing information request, payment dispute acknowledgement, incident claim acknowledgement, KYC document request, technical troubleshooting steps, and VIP escalation acknowledgement.
- Views for each department showing useful columns like requester, priority, status, vehicle type, issue category, severity, payment status, KYC status, assignee, and updated date.
- Help center categories/sections/articles for payments, claims, onboarding, technical troubleshooting, compliance/KYC, and enterprise fleet support.

Operational rules:
- Use existing selected Zendesk context where appropriate, but create missing dependencies when needed.
- Keep every record deploy-safe and incremental.
- Add dependency notes when a trigger, automation, macro, view, form, or article depends on a field, group, category, or section.
- Use clear tags such as apex_payment_issue, apex_claims_incident, apex_fleet_onboarding, apex_technical_support, apex_kyc_review, apex_enterprise_vip, urgent_safety_incident.
- Do not invent external Zendesk IDs. Reference dependencies by clear names and notes.
- Make the setup practical for a real support team, not a demo.
- Gemini should review each wave/chunk, patch safe missing details, improve titles/descriptions/body text, add missing tags/output columns/options, and surface unresolved issues without rewriting the entire batch.

planning_summary.intent:
Build a Zendesk support operating model for “Apex Mobility Finance”, a company that finances electric scooters, delivery e-bikes, and small EV fleets for gig workers and small businesses.

Business context:
Apex has these departments:
- Customer Support: first-line support for account questions, payment issues, login problems, and general requests.
- Claims & Incidents: handles damaged vehicles, theft reports, accident claims, insurance evidence, and urgent safety incidents.
- Finance Operations: handles failed payments, settlement disputes, refunds, payoff quotes, and billing corrections.
- Fleet Onboarding: helps business customers onboard multiple riders, verify documents, activate vehicles, and schedule handover.
- Technical Support: handles app bugs, GPS/device issues, charger problems, battery diagnostics, and telematics troubleshooting.
- Compliance: handles KYC document review, suspicious activity, regulatory complaints, and data/privacy requests.
- VIP / Enterprise Success: handles high-value fleet accounts, partner escalations, and white-glove support.

Create a complete Zendesk configuration in dependency order:
- Groups for the departments above, reusing existing matching groups if selected.
- Ticket fields for Department, Customer Segment, Vehicle Type, Issue Category, Incident Severity, Payment Status, KYC Status, Fleet Size, and Requested Outcome.
- Ticket forms for General Support, Claims & Incidents, Finance Operations, Fleet Onboarding, Technical Support, Compliance Review, and VIP Enterprise Support.
- Triggers to route tickets to the correct department based on form, issue category, customer segment, severity, and payment/KYC signals.
- Automations for stale urgent incidents, unresolved failed payments, pending KYC reviews, and enterprise escalations.
- Macros for first response, missing information request, payment dispute acknowledgement, incident claim acknowledgement, KYC document request, technical troubleshooting steps, and VIP escalation acknowledgement.
- Views for each department showing useful columns like requester, priority, status, vehicle type, issue category, severity, payment status, KYC status, assignee, and updated date.
- Help center categories/sections/articles for payments, claims, onboarding, technical troubleshooting, compliance/KYC, and enterprise fleet support.

Operational rules:
- Use existing selected Zendesk context where appropriate, but create missing dependencies when needed.
- Keep every record deploy-safe and incremental.
- Add dependency notes when a trigger, automation, macro, view, form, or article depends on a field, group, category, or section.
- Use clear tags such as apex_payment_issue, apex_claims_incident, apex_fleet_onboarding, apex_technical_support, apex_kyc_review, apex_enterprise_vip, urgent_safety_incident.
- Do not invent external Zendesk IDs. Reference dependencies by clear names and notes.
- Make the setup practical for a real support team, not a demo.
- Gemini should review each wave/chunk, patch safe missing details, improve titles/descriptions/body text, add missing tags/output columns/options, and surface unresolved issues without rewriting the entire batch.

BATCH-20260712-041630-D2106A.prompt:
Build a Zendesk support operating model for “Apex Mobility Finance”, a company that finances electric scooters, delivery e-bikes, and small EV fleets for gig workers and small businesses.

Business context:
Apex has these departments:
- Customer Support: first-line support for account questions, payment issues, login problems, and general requests.
- Claims & Incidents: handles damaged vehicles, theft reports, accident claims, insurance evidence, and urgent safety incidents.
- Finance Operations: handles failed payments, settlement disputes, refunds, payoff quotes, and billing corrections.
- Fleet Onboarding: helps business customers onboard multiple riders, verify documents, activate vehicles, and schedule handover.
- Technical Support: handles app bugs, GPS/device issues, charger problems, battery diagnostics, and telematics troubleshooting.
- Compliance: handles KYC document review, suspicious activity, regulatory complaints, and data/privacy requests.
- VIP / Enterprise Success: handles high-value fleet accounts, partner escalations, and white-glove support.

Create a complete Zendesk configuration in dependency order:
- Groups for the departments above, reusing existing matching groups if selected.
- Ticket fields for Department, Customer Segment, Vehicle Type, Issue Category, Incident Severity, Payment Status, KYC Status, Fleet Size, and Requested Outcome.
- Ticket forms for General Support, Claims & Incidents, Finance Operations, Fleet Onboarding, Technical Support, Compliance Review, and VIP Enterprise Support.
- Triggers to route tickets to the correct department based on form, issue category, customer segment, severity, and payment/KYC signals.
- Automations for stale urgent incidents, unresolved failed payments, pending KYC reviews, and enterprise escalations.
- Macros for first response, missing information request, payment dispute acknowledgement, incident claim acknowledgement, KYC document request, technical troubleshooting steps, and VIP escalation acknowledgement.
- Views for each department showing useful columns like requester, priority, status, vehicle type, issue category, severity, payment status, KYC status, assignee, and updated date.
- Help center categories/sections/articles for payments, claims, onboarding, technical troubleshooting, compliance/KYC, and enterprise fleet support.

Operational rules:
- Use existing selected Zendesk context where appropriate, but create missing dependencies when needed.
- Keep every record deploy-safe and incremental.
- Add dependency notes when a trigger, automation, macro, view, form, or article depends on a field, group, category, or section.
- Use clear tags such as apex_payment_issue, apex_claims_incident, apex_fleet_onboarding, apex_technical_support, apex_kyc_review, apex_enterprise_vip, urgent_safety_incident.
- Do not invent external Zendesk IDs. Reference dependencies by clear names and notes.
- Make the setup practical for a real support team, not a demo.
- Gemini should review each wave/chunk, patch safe missing details, improve titles/descriptions/body text, add missing tags/output columns/options, and surface unresolved issues without rewriting the entire batch.

Claims & Incidents: Handling Process

Our team prioritizes safety-critical incidents. Once a claim is filed, we triage based on severity (e.g., Urgent Safety Incident vs. standard damage). We will reach out for evidence verification, schedule inspections if required, and provide a resolution timeline.

Best Practices:

  • Always report safety hazards immediately via the Claims & Incidents form.
  • Attach high-resolution photos and police/insurance reports to the initial ticket.
  • Keep all correspondence within the original ticket thread to ensure the Claims specialist has the complete history.
  • Do not resume vehicle operation until authorized by our safety team if the incident involved mechanical failure or damage.

planning_summary.intent:
Build a Zendesk support operating model for “Apex Mobility Finance”, a company that finances electric scooters, delivery e-bikes, and small EV fleets for gig workers and small businesses.

Business context:
Apex has these departments:
- Customer Support: first-line support for account questions, payment issues, login problems, and general requests.
- Claims & Incidents: handles damaged vehicles, theft reports, accident claims, insurance evidence, and urgent safety incidents.
- Finance Operations: handles failed payments, settlement disputes, refunds, payoff quotes, and billing corrections.
- Fleet Onboarding: helps business customers onboard multiple riders, verify documents, activate vehicles, and schedule handover.
- Technical Support: handles app bugs, GPS/device issues, charger problems, battery diagnostics, and telematics troubleshooting.
- Compliance: handles KYC document review, suspicious activity, regulatory complaints, and data/privacy requests.
- VIP / Enterprise Success: handles high-value fleet accounts, partner escalations, and white-glove support.

Create a complete Zendesk configuration in dependency order:
- Groups for the departments above, reusing existing matching groups if selected.
- Ticket fields for Department, Customer Segment, Vehicle Type, Issue Category, Incident Severity, Payment Status, KYC Status, Fleet Size, and Requested Outcome.
- Ticket forms for General Support, Claims & Incidents, Finance Operations, Fleet Onboarding, Technical Support, Compliance Review, and VIP Enterprise Support.
- Triggers to route tickets to the correct department based on form, issue category, customer segment, severity, and payment/KYC signals.
- Automations for stale urgent incidents, unresolved failed payments, pending KYC reviews, and enterprise escalations.
- Macros for first response, missing information request, payment dispute acknowledgement, incident claim acknowledgement, KYC document request, technical troubleshooting steps, and VIP escalation acknowledgement.
- Views for each department showing useful columns like requester, priority, status, vehicle type, issue category, severity, payment status, KYC status, assignee, and updated date.
- Help center categories/sections/articles for payments, claims, onboarding, technical troubleshooting, compliance/KYC, and enterprise fleet support.

Operational rules:
- Use existing selected Zendesk context where appropriate, but create missing dependencies when needed.
- Keep every record deploy-safe and incremental.
- Add dependency notes when a trigger, automation, macro, view, form, or article depends on a field, group, category, or section.
- Use clear tags such as apex_payment_issue, apex_claims_incident, apex_fleet_onboarding, apex_technical_support, apex_kyc_review, apex_enterprise_vip, urgent_safety_incident.
- Do not invent external Zendesk IDs. Reference dependencies by clear names and notes.
- Make the setup practical for a real support team, not a demo.
- Gemini should review each wave/chunk, patch safe missing details, improve titles/descriptions/body text, add missing tags/output columns/options, and surface unresolved issues without rewriting the entire batch.

BATCH-20260712-042908-EC7F12.prompt:
Build a Zendesk support operating model for “Apex Mobility Finance”, a company that finances electric scooters, delivery e-bikes, and small EV fleets for gig workers and small businesses.

Business context:
Apex has these departments:
- Customer Support: first-line support for account questions, payment issues, login problems, and general requests.
- Claims & Incidents: handles damaged vehicles, theft reports, accident claims, insurance evidence, and urgent safety incidents.
- Finance Operations: handles failed payments, settlement disputes, refunds, payoff quotes, and billing corrections.
- Fleet Onboarding: helps business customers onboard multiple riders, verify documents, activate vehicles, and schedule handover.
- Technical Support: handles app bugs, GPS/device issues, charger problems, battery diagnostics, and telematics troubleshooting.
- Compliance: handles KYC document review, suspicious activity, regulatory complaints, and data/privacy requests.
- VIP / Enterprise Success: handles high-value fleet accounts, partner escalations, and white-glove support.

Create a complete Zendesk configuration in dependency order:
- Groups for the departments above, reusing existing matching groups if selected.
- Ticket fields for Department, Customer Segment, Vehicle Type, Issue Category, Incident Severity, Payment Status, KYC Status, Fleet Size, and Requested Outcome.
- Ticket forms for General Support, Claims & Incidents, Finance Operations, Fleet Onboarding, Technical Support, Compliance Review, and VIP Enterprise Support.
- Triggers to route tickets to the correct department based on form, issue category, customer segment, severity, and payment/KYC signals.
- Automations for stale urgent incidents, unresolved failed payments, pending KYC reviews, and enterprise escalations.
- Macros for first response, missing information request, payment dispute acknowledgement, incident claim acknowledgement, KYC document request, technical troubleshooting steps, and VIP escalation acknowledgement.
- Views for each department showing useful columns like requester, priority, status, vehicle type, issue category, severity, payment status, KYC status, assignee, and updated date.
- Help center categories/sections/articles for payments, claims, onboarding, technical troubleshooting, compliance/KYC, and enterprise fleet support.

Operational rules:
- Use existing selected Zendesk context where appropriate, but create missing dependencies when needed.
- Keep every record deploy-safe and incremental.
- Add dependency notes when a trigger, automation, macro, view, form, or article depends on a field, group, category, or section.
- Use clear tags such as apex_payment_issue, apex_claims_incident, apex_fleet_onboarding, apex_technical_support, apex_kyc_review, apex_enterprise_vip, urgent_safety_incident.
- Do not invent external Zendesk IDs. Reference dependencies by clear names and notes.
- Make the setup practical for a real support team, not a demo.
- Gemini should review each wave/chunk, patch safe missing details, improve titles/descriptions/body text, add missing tags/output columns/options, and surface unresolved issues without rewriting the entire batch.

planning_summary.intent:
Build a Zendesk support operating model for “Apex Mobility Finance”, a company that finances electric scooters, delivery e-bikes, and small EV fleets for gig workers and small businesses.

Business context:
Apex has these departments:
- Customer Support: first-line support for account questions, payment issues, login problems, and general requests.
- Claims & Incidents: handles damaged vehicles, theft reports, accident claims, insurance evidence, and urgent safety incidents.
- Finance Operations: handles failed payments, settlement disputes, refunds, payoff quotes, and billing corrections.
- Fleet Onboarding: helps business customers onboard multiple riders, verify documents, activate vehicles, and schedule handover.
- Technical Support: handles app bugs, GPS/device issues, charger problems, battery diagnostics, and telematics troubleshooting.
- Compliance: handles KYC document review, suspicious activity, regulatory complaints, and data/privacy requests.
- VIP / Enterprise Success: handles high-value fleet accounts, partner escalations, and white-glove support.

Create a complete Zendesk configuration in dependency order:
- Groups for the departments above, reusing existing matching groups if selected.
- Ticket fields for Department, Customer Segment, Vehicle Type, Issue Category, Incident Severity, Payment Status, KYC Status, Fleet Size, and Requested Outcome.
- Ticket forms for General Support, Claims & Incidents, Finance Operations, Fleet Onboarding, Technical Support, Compliance Review, and VIP Enterprise Support.
- Triggers to route tickets to the correct department based on form, issue category, customer segment, severity, and payment/KYC signals.
- Automations for stale urgent incidents, unresolved failed payments, pending KYC reviews, and enterprise escalations.
- Macros for first response, missing information request, payment dispute acknowledgement, incident claim acknowledgement, KYC document request, technical troubleshooting steps, and VIP escalation acknowledgement.
- Views for each department showing useful columns like requester, priority, status, vehicle type, issue category, severity, payment status, KYC status, assignee, and updated date.
- Help center categories/sections/articles for payments, claims, onboarding, technical troubleshooting, compliance/KYC, and enterprise fleet support.

Operational rules:
- Use existing selected Zendesk context where appropriate, but create missing dependencies when needed.
- Keep every record deploy-safe and incremental.
- Add dependency notes when a trigger, automation, macro, view, form, or article depends on a field, group, category, or section.
- Use clear tags such as apex_payment_issue, apex_claims_incident, apex_fleet_onboarding, apex_technical_support, apex_kyc_review, apex_enterprise_vip, urgent_safety_incident.
- Do not invent external Zendesk IDs. Reference dependencies by clear names and notes.
- Make the setup practical for a real support team, not a demo.
- Gemini should review each wave/chunk, patch safe missing details, improve titles/descriptions/body text, add missing tags/output columns/options, and surface unresolved issues without rewriting the entire batch.

BATCH-20260712-043953-093915.prompt:
Build a Zendesk support operating model for “Apex Mobility Finance”, a company that finances electric scooters, delivery e-bikes, and small EV fleets for gig workers and small businesses.

Business context:
Apex has these departments:
- Customer Support: first-line support for account questions, payment issues, login problems, and general requests.
- Claims & Incidents: handles damaged vehicles, theft reports, accident claims, insurance evidence, and urgent safety incidents.
- Finance Operations: handles failed payments, settlement disputes, refunds, payoff quotes, and billing corrections.
- Fleet Onboarding: helps business customers onboard multiple riders, verify documents, activate vehicles, and schedule handover.
- Technical Support: handles app bugs, GPS/device issues, charger problems, battery diagnostics, and telematics troubleshooting.
- Compliance: handles KYC document review, suspicious activity, regulatory complaints, and data/privacy requests.
- VIP / Enterprise Success: handles high-value fleet accounts, partner escalations, and white-glove support.

Create a complete Zendesk configuration in dependency order:
- Groups for the departments above, reusing existing matching groups if selected.
- Ticket fields for Department, Customer Segment, Vehicle Type, Issue Category, Incident Severity, Payment Status, KYC Status, Fleet Size, and Requested Outcome.
- Ticket forms for General Support, Claims & Incidents, Finance Operations, Fleet Onboarding, Technical Support, Compliance Review, and VIP Enterprise Support.
- Triggers to route tickets to the correct department based on form, issue category, customer segment, severity, and payment/KYC signals.
- Automations for stale urgent incidents, unresolved failed payments, pending KYC reviews, and enterprise escalations.
- Macros for first response, missing information request, payment dispute acknowledgement, incident claim acknowledgement, KYC document request, technical troubleshooting steps, and VIP escalation acknowledgement.
- Views for each department showing useful columns like requester, priority, status, vehicle type, issue category, severity, payment status, KYC status, assignee, and updated date.
- Help center categories/sections/articles for payments, claims, onboarding, technical troubleshooting, compliance/KYC, and enterprise fleet support.

Operational rules:
- Use existing selected Zendesk context where appropriate, but create missing dependencies when needed.
- Keep every record deploy-safe and incremental.
- Add dependency notes when a trigger, automation, macro, view, form, or article depends on a field, group, category, or section.
- Use clear tags such as apex_payment_issue, apex_claims_incident, apex_fleet_onboarding, apex_technical_support, apex_kyc_review, apex_enterprise_vip, urgent_safety_incident.
- Do not invent external Zendesk IDs. Reference dependencies by clear names and notes.
- Make the setup practical for a real support team, not a demo.
- Gemini should review each wave/chunk, patch safe missing details, improve titles/descriptions/body text, add missing tags/output columns/options, and surface unresolved issues without rewriting the entire batch.

The Compliance team will prioritize requests based on regulatory severity. We will reach out via this ticket if additional documentation is required.

planning_summary.intent:
Build a Zendesk support operating model for “Apex Mobility Finance”, a company that finances electric scooters, delivery e-bikes, and small EV fleets for gig workers and small businesses.

Business context:
Apex has these departments:
- Customer Support: first-line support for account questions, payment issues, login problems, and general requests.
- Claims & Incidents: handles damaged vehicles, theft reports, accident claims, insurance evidence, and urgent safety incidents.
- Finance Operations: handles failed payments, settlement disputes, refunds, payoff quotes, and billing corrections.
- Fleet Onboarding: helps business customers onboard multiple riders, verify documents, activate vehicles, and schedule handover.
- Technical Support: handles app bugs, GPS/device issues, charger problems, battery diagnostics, and telematics troubleshooting.
- Compliance: handles KYC document review, suspicious activity, regulatory complaints, and data/privacy requests.
- VIP / Enterprise Success: handles high-value fleet accounts, partner escalations, and white-glove support.

Create a complete Zendesk configuration in dependency order:
- Groups for the departments above, reusing existing matching groups if selected.
- Ticket fields for Department, Customer Segment, Vehicle Type, Issue Category, Incident Severity, Payment Status, KYC Status, Fleet Size, and Requested Outcome.
- Ticket forms for General Support, Claims & Incidents, Finance Operations, Fleet Onboarding, Technical Support, Compliance Review, and VIP Enterprise Support.
- Triggers to route tickets to the correct department based on form, issue category, customer segment, severity, and payment/KYC signals.
- Automations for stale urgent incidents, unresolved failed payments, pending KYC reviews, and enterprise escalations.
- Macros for first response, missing information request, payment dispute acknowledgement, incident claim acknowledgement, KYC document request, technical troubleshooting steps, and VIP escalation acknowledgement.
- Views for each department showing useful columns like requester, priority, status, vehicle type, issue category, severity, payment status, KYC status, assignee, and updated date.
- Help center categories/sections/articles for payments, claims, onboarding, technical troubleshooting, compliance/KYC, and enterprise fleet support.

Operational rules:
- Use existing selected Zendesk context where appropriate, but create missing dependencies when needed.
- Keep every record deploy-safe and incremental.
- Add dependency notes when a trigger, automation, macro, view, form, or article depends on a field, group, category, or section.
- Use clear tags such as apex_payment_issue, apex_claims_incident, apex_fleet_onboarding, apex_technical_support, apex_kyc_review, apex_enterprise_vip, urgent_safety_incident.
- Do not invent external Zendesk IDs. Reference dependencies by clear names and notes.
- Make the setup practical for a real support team, not a demo.
- Gemini should review each wave/chunk, patch safe missing details, improve titles/descriptions/body text, add missing tags/output columns/options, and surface unresolved issues without rewriting the entire batch.
